stories.headline: Trump bans CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from White House press access
stories.body:
President Donald Trump banned CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House on Friday [c8]. He posted on Truth Social that the outlets report fake news [c15]. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that banned outlets purposely write negative news [c17]. He said they do this to try to diminish Republicans [c17]. Trump said he does not want them in his office [c2]. He added that he wants the ban to go as far as possible [c2]. Trump also said he intends to sue all three outlets [c3].

The banned organizations and rights groups quickly responded to the decision. CNN called the ban an illegal assault on constitutionally-protected press freedoms [c9]. Politico said it will continue to report fairly on the White House [c10]. It added that it will defend its First Amendment rights [c10]. Bruce Brown of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press called the move flatly unconstitutional [c14]. Jameel Jaffer of the Knight First Amendment Institute said excluding journalists based on viewpoint is unconstitutional [c13]. Amnesty International accused the administration of trying to stifle scrutiny [c20]. Reporters Without Borders said it is exploring legal avenues to respond [c18].

vocab.meaning: against the rules set in a country's constitution

stories.headline: US and Denmark reach security agreement regarding Greenland
stories.body:
The United States, Denmark, and Greenland agreed on Friday to sign a new Arctic security pact [c7, c21]. The three leaders announced they expect to sign the deal next week at the United Nations General Assembly [c7, c21]. Chairman of the Greenland Government Jens-Frederik Nielsen confirmed the upcoming agreement [c24]. US President Donald Trump posted about the deal on Truth Social [c22]. Trump said the agreement comes at no cost to the United States [c22]. He called the security pact an "Infinite Life" agreement with no end date [c29].

Trump posted that plans will start immediately to build a large military presence in parts of Greenland [c28]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the agreement a historic deal [c25]. Rubio said it is a huge win for the United States and the American people [c25]. An anonymous US State Department official shared details about the terms [c26]. The official said the deal explicitly guarantees complete ability for the US to defend the American continent [c26]. This includes permanent military access across Greenland [c26]. It also grants permanent basing rights and overflight rights [c26].

The US official said the agreement blocks other world powers [c27]. The official said it guarantees China and Russia cannot set up military bases in Greenland [c27]. The official added that neither country can send troops to Greenland [c27]. Currently, the United States maintains a military installation at Pituffik Space Base in Greenland [c30]. That facility operates under existing defense arrangements with Denmark [c30].

Denmark Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen spoke about the value of the pact [c23]. Frederiksen said the deal strengthens common security in the Arctic and North Atlantic area [c23]. She noted that the deal recognizes the sovereignty of the Kingdom [c23]. She added that it respects Greenlandic self-determination [c23].

vocab.meaning: the authority of a nation to govern itself
the right of an aircraft to fly through foreign airspace

stories.headline: Suicide bombing and shooting at Pakistan mosque kill at least 21
stories.body:
A suicide bomber and gunmen attacked a mosque near police offices in Pakistan's Kohat district [c31]. The vehicle bomb explosion and shooting killed at least 21 people [c31]. The attack also injured 80 other people [c31]. Fifteen police officers were among those killed in the mosque attack [c36]. A four-year-old child was also killed in the bombing [c36]. Police killed six armed gunmen and one suicide bomber during the compound attack [c32].

Police in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa suggested a faction of Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan carried out the attack [c37]. UN Secretary-General António Guterres strongly condemned the bombing [c38]. Guterres said that attacks targeting places of worship are unacceptable [c38].

The attack comes during broader security clashes across Pakistan. A roadside bomb in Hangu district killed six soldiers on Thursday [c33]. Pakistani troops killed 10 suspected Taliban militants during raids on Thursday [c34]. Security forces also killed seven militants in Balochistan province [c39]. Earlier in February, a suicide bombing at an Islamabad mosque killed at least 31 people [c40]. Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif [c35]. They discussed rising tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan [c35].

vocab.meaning: people who use violent methods to achieve political goals
a small dissenting group within a larger organization

stories.headline: Protests erupt in Nigeria after 37 suspected illegal miners die in custody
stories.body:
Thirty-seven suspected illegal gold miners died in custody in Minna, Nigeria [c41]. The men were held in a cell run by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps [c41]. An intelligence report showed that overcrowding and poor ventilation likely caused the deaths [c43]. The agency initially claimed a diphtheria outbreak might be responsible [c48]. It later said the cause of death was unconfirmed [c48]. The detainees were buried on Thursday without forensic examinations [c46].

The deaths triggered angry street protests in Minna. Security forces fired tear gas and opened fire on demonstrators [c42, c49]. Niger State Governor Umar Bago declared three days of mourning [c44]. He imposed a 24-hour curfew following violent attacks on government buildings [c50]. Governor Bago also postponed the start of election campaigning [c44].

Nigeria Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo ordered an investigation [c45]. He immediately suspended Niger state agency commandant Suberu Siyaka Aniviye [c45]. Agency spokesperson Babawale Afolabi said over 50 people were arrested in raids before the deaths [c47].

vocab.meaning: people held in official custody or prison
the supply of fresh air into a closed space

stories.headline: Bank of Japan raises interest rate to 1.25 percent
stories.body:
The Bank of Japan raised its target interest rate to 1.25 percent on Friday [c51, c54]. Policy makers voted 7-2 to increase the rate by 25 basis points [c51]. The move brings borrowing costs in Japan to their highest level since 1995 [c54]. Following the announcement, the Japanese yen fell against the US dollar [c52].

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda discussed future policy after the decision [c55]. Ueda said he would not rule out back-to-back interest rate hikes [c55]. He noted that future decisions depend on how price conditions develop [c55]. Inflation in Japan stood at 1.9 percent in August [c56].

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned currency traders not to bet against the yen [c57]. Bessent said he had insight into Japanese policy actions [c57]. In late July, the US Treasury sold at least $10 billion in euros to buy yen [c58]. That intervention aimed to support the Japanese currency [c58]. The Bank of England voted to keep UK interest rates unchanged at 3.75 percent [c59].

vocab.meaning: a general increase in prices over time
action taken to influence or alter an economic outcome

stories.headline: Mamata Banerjee petitions Supreme Court after Election Commission freezes TMC symbol
stories.body:
Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee challenged an Election Commission ruling in the Supreme Court [c60]. Her Trinamool Congress faction filed the petition on September 18, 2026 [c60]. The filing follows an interim order issued by the Election Commission of India on September 17 [c61]. That order froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and symbol [c61]. The decision applies to upcoming West Bengal Assembly byelections in Nandigram and Rejinagar [c61].

The Election Commission gave new names and symbols to both competing party factions [c62]. Mamata Banerjee's group received the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' [c62]. Her faction was given a 'football player' symbol [c62]. A rival faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee received the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' [c62]. The commission allotted an 'envelope' symbol to Ritabrata Banerjee's group [c62]. Both factions are recognized as political parties in West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Tripura [c66].

Mamata Banerjee described losing her party's original name and symbol as a black day in democratic history [c65]. She originally founded the All India Trinamool Congress in 1998 [c64]. She created the party after splitting from the Indian National Congress [c64]. She had personally hand-drew the original 'Jora Ghas Phool' symbol [c64]. In her court filing, her faction highlighted long delays in disqualification proceedings [c63]. Those proceedings against 10 rebel legislators remain pending before the West Bengal Assembly Speaker [c63].

The legal battle follows severe internal party rebellions. Nearly 60 out of 80 Trinamool Congress state lawmakers rebelled after May elections [c70]. In June 2026, 20 out of 28 party members in the Lok Sabha merged with another party [c71]. They joined the Tripura-based Nationalist Citizens Party of India [c71].

Following the symbol ruling, political plans for upcoming elections shifted. Sanchita Pradhan Dey was initially chosen as candidate for Mamata Banerjee's faction in Nandigram [c68]. However, Dey withdrew her nomination [c68]. Mamata Banerjee then announced her faction would not contest the Nandigram seat [c67]. Instead, her group backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan [c67]. On September 18, 2026, police arrested Pradhan in connection with a 2007 murder case [c69].

vocab.meaning: a formal written request appealing to a court of law

stories.headline: US President Donald Trump signs Russia sanctions law targeting energy importers
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump signed a new sanctions bill into law on Friday [c72]. The legislation is called the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 [c72]. Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who named the bill, died in July 2026 [c73]. The US Senate passed the bill 86-11 in August [c74]. The House of Representatives later approved it in a 262-159 vote [c74].

The law gives the US president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent [c75]. These tariffs apply to imports from the five largest buyers of Russian oil or natural gas [c75]. The targets include India and China [c75]. Countries importing under 15 percent of Russia's natural gas exports may get exemptions [c78]. To qualify, they must take significant steps to reduce imports [c78].

India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a warning about the new law [c77]. It said the sanctions could hurt India-US bilateral relations [c77]. The ministry added that the law could impact global energy markets [c77]. The bill also extends the Iran Sanctions Act for five more years [c76].

vocab.meaning: taxes placed by a government on imported goods
special permissions to not follow a requirement

stories.headline: India rejects Pakistan's account of naval warship collision in Arabian Sea
stories.body:
India has rejected Pakistan's allegations regarding a collision between two warships in the Arabian Sea [c81]. The incident occurred on September 15, 2026, between Indian warship INS Kolkata and Pakistani vessel PNS Hunain [c81]. India summoned Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires Saad Warraich to lodge a protest [c82]. Foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said PNS Hunain performed a dangerous overtaking manoeuvre [c83]. He said this violated a 1991 bilateral agreement requiring warships to stay three nautical miles apart [c83].

INS Kolkata sustained no major damage and remained at sea [c84]. PNS Hunain was observed returning to harbour after sustaining damage [c84]. Pakistan gave a conflicting account of the collision. Pakistan summoned Indian Charge d'Affaires Satyanjal Pandey [c85]. It alleged that aggressive manoeuvres by the Indian warship inside Pakistan's economic zone caused the crash [c85].

The last recorded collision between the two navies happened in 2011 [c86]. In that incident, INS Godavari was marginally damaged by PNS Babur during anti-piracy operations [c86].

vocab.meaning: claims that someone has committed a wrong action
a movement requiring skill and control
